records.title: Language model-guided anticipation and discovery of mammalian metabolites
records.sample_size_raw: For isotope tracing, two mice were infused for each tracer in an exploratory fashion to identify the presence or absence of labeling in product metabolites. For purified and chow diets, four mice were fed the respective diets. Dietary intake, both in timing and quantity, can vary between mice, such that four mice was assessed to be the minimum sample size needed to evaluate changes between groups. For the antibiotics treatment experiment we used 3-4 mice per group, as based on pilot studies we found that number to be sufficient for detecting changes in metabolite levels between the groups.

records.title: Baby-to-baby strain transmission shapes the developing gut microbiome
records.sample_size_raw: We collected and utilized n=1013 fecal metagenomes from N=134 participants in this longitudinal study. As this was an observational, ecologically constrained study focusing on the first year of nursery, we did not perform a formal a priori cohort size calculation. Instead, our strategy was based on maximum achievable recruitment within the existing units in each nursery. We targeted the entire available population across three large-sized nurseries (with two classes each, with a maximum capacity of 12 babies per class). We successfully recruited in the study 43 babies out of the 71 enrolled in these specific units, representing more than 60% of the eligible population. In addition, we recruited 3-4 educators per nursery, which represented the maximum number of staff directly attending these babies (2 educators per class). This approach, together with dense longitudinal sample collection, allowed us to successfully enroll a sufficient and robust sample size for the comparative analyses of strain sharing both within and between the defined nursery groups, capturing the majority of the relevant social interactions. records.title: Critical role for a high-plasticity cell state in lung cancer
records.sample_size_raw: No sample size calculation was performed for the given animal studies. For Slc4a11-MCD/+, Hopx-MACD/+, Rosa26-CreERT2, Rosa26-mTmG/+ and Hipp11-GGCB/+ studies, we were restricted by the number of mice with the correct genotype to be included in the experimental groups. For transplantation studies, initial numbers of mice for each group were n>5, which we felt should suffice to show a statistical difference if the effect size was robust and significantly large. For animal studies and other experiments, sample sizes were determined based on our prior experience with similar models, sufficient to detect biologically meaningful differences while minimizing animal use.

records.title: Rete ridges form via evolutionarily distinct mechanisms in mammalian skin
records.sample_size_raw: No sample size calculations were performed. A minimum of 3 or more biological replicates, and a mix of males and females, were obtained when possible, however some timepoints within our human or pig sample sets only consisted of 1-2 biological replicates due to model limitations (e.g. initial pig litter size), which are clearly delineated in the figure legends. In mouse experiments, multiple litters and a mix of male and female individuals were used when possible with specifics included in the figure legends or methods section. In pig experiments, multiple litters were used when possible with specifics included in the figure legends or methods section. Sample sizes in this study are comparable to other studies in our field.
